cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Ninth concept. One-to-one replication of the GLP-1 SOS Bristol chart ad (FB 2071335783784246), third creative ported from this direct competitor. 1:1 square, cream field, bold dark-green headline with a hand-drawn red underline swoosh, seven-row chart with type label left, rendering centre and descriptor right, types 3 and 4 circled together in a loose red oval, bold sub-line lower left, green CTA button, jar lower right. cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: MARGIN FIX · 2026-08-26
cards.text:
The first pass ran the headline nearly edge to edge and hard against the top of the frame, and the chart rules reached the sides.

Fixed by making the margin rule apply to EVERY ELEMENT rather than just the type, and by breaking each headline onto two lines so it could not stretch:

'Leave a wide band of completely empty cream around all four sides, like a generous printed page margin. No text, no chart rule, no red mark and no product comes closer to any edge than one eighth of the image width. Clear empty band across the very top before the headline begins and across the very bottom. Size everything down so the entire composition sits comfortably inside those margins.'

THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: on a dense layout, a margin instruction aimed only at the headline gets obeyed for the headline and ignored by the chart rules and the product. Name the elements, or say 'every element.'

Forcing the headline onto TWO LINES is the other half. A single long line will always stretch toward the edges no matter what the margin rule says, because the model treats the line break as fixed and the width as negotiable.

cards.title: WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH RUNNING
cards.text:
Every other concept in this set TELLS her something. This one asks a question she has to answer with her own body, then shows her the answer is abnormal.

The Bristol scale is already circulating in GLP-1 groups, so a large part of the audience has half-seen it. Putting it in front of her with the GLP-1 framing attached is the difference between 'here is a chart' and 'here is why your chart moved.'

It also does the job Brooks named: IT PROVES A GLP-1 STOMACH IS A DIFFERENT STOMACH. Not broken, not her fault, just sitting somewhere else on a scale that already exists. That reframing is the whole belief shift, and it lands faster in a chart than in three paragraphs of copy.

cards.title: PRODUCTION NOTE · THE CONTENT FILTER
cards.text:
GPT Image 2 refuses prompts that describe stool literally.

Every row here was specified as BROWN MODELLING CLAY in the shape required: pebbles, a lumpy sausage, a cracked sausage, a smooth tapered sausage, soft rounded blobs, ragged pieces, a flat glossy puddle.

The render is photographically identical to what a literal description would have produced, and every roll cleared. Same workaround that unblocked the colon interiors in MOT-MECHANISM-3D-01.

THE ON-IMAGE WORD 'poop' RENDERS FINE. It is the visual description that trips the filter, not the copy.

cards.title: SHARED PRIMARY TEXT
cards.text:
There is a chart for this, and if you have spent any time in a GLP-1 group you have probably already scrolled past it.

Seven types, from hard pellets down to loose. Three and four are the smooth, easy middle, and that is what normal looks like. Here is the part that rarely gets said when the prescription is written: a GLP-1 pushes you up the chart, toward one and two.

Nothing is broken. The medication slows the whole digestive system down on purpose, because that is how it quiets your appetite. But slower transit means more time for water to be pulled back out along the way. Harder, drier, pellets and lumps instead of smooth and easy. Your stomach on a GLP-1 is not the stomach you had before it, and the chart is where you can actually see that.

It is also why the harsh fixes miss. Forcing a contraction in a system the medication is deliberately quieting gets you cramping and a lurch toward the far end of the chart. Not the middle.

Motilli works on the reason instead. Your colon contracts on a signal called butyrate, made by the bacteria in your colon out of the fiber that reaches them. Slow everything down and less reaches them, the colony thins out, and the signal fades. Concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of apigenin, which barely absorbs into your bloodstream and so stays down in the colon where the problem is. Plus a fine soluble prebiotic fiber to feed those bacteria back up.

Nothing is forced, so there is no cramping and no urgency. The first few days are quiet, and it fills in over the following weeks.

None of it touches your weight loss. Weight loss lives in the brain and the appetite. This lives in the colon. Two separate systems, so you rebuild one and stay on the other.

Two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Sixty in a bottle. Third-party tested, lab results posted.

Ninety days to decide. Email inside ninety days and every dollar comes back, no return required.

One honest note. This is support for the slowed, backed-up side of the chart. If things are running loose, or anything is severe or persistent, that is a conversation for your doctor. Never stop a prescribed medication without their guidance.

cards.title: COMPETITOR DISCIPLINE
cards.text:
Third creative ported from this advertiser.

THEIR HEADLINE IS THEIRS. 'Your poop can tell you a lot.' stays with them. All three of ours are written fresh, and all three carry the GLP-1 framing their headline leaves to the body copy.

THEIR BODY COPY names magnesium, a Tri-Phase Blend, ginger, peppermint, B12, iron and B6. None of that is in our bottle and none of it appears in ours.

THEIR SOCIAL PROOF is '4.8 stars, 55,000+ GLP-1 users' plus a named verified reviewer. We have none of that verified, so none of it is anywhere in ours. No stars, no counts, no testimonial.

WE KEPT THEIR HONEST-NOTE BEAT, because it is genuinely good practice on this category and it is true for us too.

THEIR BOTTLE was never passed as a reference image. Our jar is the only product input.

cards.title: FRAME QA · all three, after the margin fix
cards.text:
Margins: PASS. Clear empty cream band on all four sides in all three. Headline, chart rules, red oval, button and jar all sit inside. Nothing touching an edge.

Headline: PASS. Two lines, spelled exactly, dark green, red hand-drawn underline swoosh present, noticeably narrower than the chart.

Chart: PASS. Exactly seven rows. Type 1 through Type 7 left, correct rendering centre, correct descriptor right.

Red oval: PASS. One loose hand-drawn oval enclosing rows 3 and 4 together in all three. Not four rows, not two separate ovals.

Descriptors: PASS. Hard pellets / Lumpy log / Cracked log / Smooth snake / Soft blobs / Mushy pieces / Loose stool.

Sub-line and button: PASS. Three lines plus solid dark green button with white 'Try Motilli'.

Jar: PASS. motilli wordmark and CELERY JUICE FIBER GUMMIES legible.

No invented badges, prices, star ratings, review counts or percentages.

cards.title: AUDIT
cards.text:
Law 2: no invented study, percentage, doctor, review count or customer quote. The Bristol scale is an established clinical scale, not a sourced statistic.

Law 6: competitor intelligence stayed a brief direction. No line of their copy appears in ours and no comparison is drawn.

Law 9: no em dashes, no negation-affirmation beats, no parallel stacks, no rhetorical openers.

Two separate systems: present.

Swap test: PASS. Drop a laxative into this ad and both the sub-line and the mechanism paragraph argue against it.

Shelf life: evergreen.

CLAIM RISK: low on imagery, moderate on category. No body shots, no before-and-after. Worth confirming the account is comfortable running the word on-image before it spends.

VERIFY BEFORE LAUNCH: the 90-day no-return-required guarantee wording against the live policy page.
